title: Privacy starts with the data you do not collect
summary: Design an experiment with minimal records and deliberate retention.

sections.title: Reduce exposure at collection time
paragraphs: Before collecting a field, explain what decision it supports and how long it is needed. A lesson recommendation experiment may need topic choices and completion counts, but not a learner’s private messages. Reducing fields simplifies both the system and its risk.

A hash is not automatic anonymization. Predictable identifiers such as email addresses can be guessed and hashed again. Combining several harmless-looking attributes may also identify someone. Use precise terms such as pseudonymized when re-identification remains possible.

sections.title: Redaction is one layer
paragraphs: Pattern matching can remove obvious identifiers from logs, but misses unusual formatting and context-dependent personal information. Treat it as a convenience layer, not proof that text is safe to publish.

Prefer structured diagnostic events: operation name, duration, status, and a request ID. Restrict log access and choose a retention window. Apply the same care to prompts, retrieved passages, generated outputs, and evaluation datasets.

code.source:
import re
text = "Contact learner@example.test about lesson 3."
redacted = re.sub(r"[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}", "[email removed]", text)
event = {"operation": "lesson_search", "status": "ok", "duration_ms": 12}
print(redacted)
print(event)
code.explanation: The email is invented. The regular expression demonstrates a narrow pattern and should not be presented as comprehensive anonymization.

steps: List five fields you might collect.
Remove fields that are not required to answer a concrete product question.
Choose a retention period and explain who needs access.
practice.solution: For a completion counter, lesson ID and a coarse date may be sufficient. A raw prompt, email address, and full IP address are not automatically necessary. Requirements vary, so document the purpose rather than collecting everything by default.
practice.expected: The example email is replaced, while the structured event contains no message text.

quiz.question: Does replacing email addresses make arbitrary text anonymous?
options: Yes, email is the only identifier
No, other identifiers and contextual clues can remain
Only if the replacement string is long
quiz.explanation: Anonymity is a property of the remaining information and re-identification risk, not one regex substitution.
